bug_description.normalized: The exact 3150-byte witness reproduces an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 3 in `modules/codec/svcdsub.c:550` (`SVCDSubRenderImage`). Stage 01's saved stack shows the MPEG-PS path `Demux -> es_out_Send -> EsOutSend -> test_decoder_process -> Decode` reaching the SVCD subtitle decoder. Static replay of `Reassemble()` over the staged witness identifies a complete subtitle packet whose `ParseHeader()` bytes set `p_sys->i_width=64`, `p_sys->i_height=384`, and `p_sys->second_field_offset=1`; `DecodePacket()` therefore allocates a 64x384 `VLC_CODEC_YUVP` picture, i.e. a 24576-byte Y plane. Static replay of `SVCDSubRenderImage()` over that extracted image payload shows the crash occurs in the odd-field pass at row 383, column 62 when the zero-color RLE token yields `i_count=2`. The buggy clamp `__MIN(i_count, p_sys->i_width - i_column)` leaves `i_count` at 2 even though the subsequent `memset()` writes `i_count + 1 = 3` bytes, so the write starts at Y-plane offset 24574 and crosses one byte past the 24576-byte allocation end. The staged `patch.diff` does not touch `modules/codec/svcdsub.c`, so this causal chain is grounded in the vulnerable source, the staged witness, and the saved ASan trace rather than the mismatched patch text.

source.description: First project-side statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled decoder state from the demuxed subtitle packet. `ParseHeader()` reads the subtitle image width and height from `p_block->p_buffer`, and those values later determine both the picture allocation size and the remaining-pixels term used by the buggy clamp.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 3150-byte MPEG Program Stream witness (sha256 `4f2d52d3696a34bcfbaa35e9e4279e98224f6fb4abffeb0181c6cd6449597965`). Stage 01's saved stack shows `modules/demux/mpeg/ps.c:656` dispatching a demuxed packet through `EsOutSend` and `test_decoder_process` into `Decode()`. Static replay of the witness's only `0x000001bd` PES packet at file offset 8 shows VLC advances 16 header bytes before `Reassemble()` sees decoder payload `00 ff 80 01 6d` at file offset 24; after the 5-byte subtitle-packet header is stripped, `ParseHeader()` consumes bytes starting at offset 29, where `GETINT16` reads `0x0040` and `0x0180` as width 64 and height 384.

sink.description: ASan-observed sink. The decoder zero-fills `i_count + 1` pixels starting at the current destination position in the subtitle picture plane. On the reproducing run this `memset()` crosses the heap allocation created for the subtitle image buffer.
sink.note: Static replay of the extracted odd-field path plus the saved ASan report closes the sink state: the crashing token executes on `i_row=383`, `i_column=62` with `Y_PITCH=64` and `i_count=2`, so line 550 calls `memset(&p_dest[383 * 64 + 62], 0, 3)`. That starts at byte offset 24574 of the 24576-byte Y-plane allocation and makes the first invalid byte land exactly at 24576, matching ASan's `WRITE of size 3` at the allocation end.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `i_count` in this branch is the run-length minus one, but the code clips it against the full number of pixels remaining in the row. On the reproduced path `i_column` is 62 and `p_sys->i_width` is 64, so the clamp leaves `i_count` at 2 and the next `memset(..., i_count + 1)` still spans one byte past the row and allocation boundary.

tainted_value_origin.description: The crashing RLE token is read directly from the attacker-controlled compressed subtitle image. Static replay of the odd-field bitstream beginning at `i_image_offset + second_field_offset` shows the crash-driving read occurs on row 383, column 62: `bs_read(&bs, 2)` returns color 0 and the next `bs_read(&bs, 2)` returns `i_count = 2`, which flows into both the buggy clamp at line 549 and the sink size `i_count + 1` at line 550.

parser_admitted.description: After MPEG-PS demux has dispatched the packet and `EsOutSend` has selected the decoder, this call enters `modules/codec/svcdsub.c::Decode` on the reproducing path. The saved stack confirms the chain `Demux -> es_out_Send -> EsOutSend -> test_decoder_process -> Decode`.

packet_reassembled.description: Static replay of the witness's only `0x000001bd` PES packet at file offset 8 shows VLC strips a 16-byte PES header before `Reassemble()` receives decoder payload `00 ff 80 01 6d` at file offset 24. After the 5-byte subtitle-packet header is stripped, `ParseHeader()` sees bytes beginning at offset 29 (`70 f3 a0 80 bd 36 23 b6 00 40 01 80 ...`).

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness wraps the witness bytes in an in-memory VLC stream and runs the demux pipeline over that stream.
The MPEG Program Stream demux extracts a packet from the witness and forwards it through `es_out_Send()` into the subtitle decoder path seen in the saved crash stack.

On the first complete subtitle packet, `ParseHeader()` reads attacker-controlled geometry and image-layout fields from the SVCD subtitle header and stores `p_sys->i_width=64`, `p_sys->i_height=384`, `p_sys->i_image_offset=31`, and `p_sys->second_field_offset=1` in `decoder_sys_t`.
The decoder uses that geometry to configure a `YUVP` subtitle format and allocate a 64x384 heap-backed subtitle picture whose Y plane is 24576 bytes.

In the odd-field pass starting at `i_image_offset + second_field_offset`, the zero-color RLE token at row 383 column 62 is clamped with the off-by-one rule and then `memset(..., 3)` overruns the end of the Y plane by one byte.

fine_trace.note: Source. Static replay of `Reassemble()` over the staged witness shows these `GETINT16` calls read `0x0040` and `0x0180`, so attacker input fixes `p_sys->i_width=64` and `p_sys->i_height=384`.

fine_trace.code: p_sys->second_field_offset = GETINT16(p); p_sys->i_image_offset  = p - p_block->p_buffer; p_sys->i_image_length  = p_sys->i_spu_size - p_sys->i_image_offset;
fine_trace.note: The same attacker-controlled header sets `p_sys->second_field_offset=1` and records `p_sys->i_image_offset=31`, so the compressed subtitle image begins 31 bytes into the reassembled block and the odd-field bitstream starts one byte after the even-field bitstream.

fine_trace.code: fmt.i_width = fmt.i_visible_width = p_sys->i_width; fmt.i_height = fmt.i_visible_height = p_sys->i_height;
fine_trace.note: DecodePacket copies the attacker-chosen geometry into the subtitle picture format, so the destination surface is configured as 64 by 384 pixels.

fine_trace.code: p->i_lines = height * h->num / h->den; p->i_pitch = width * w->num / w->den * p_dsc->pixel_size; p->i_visible_pitch = (fmt->i_visible_width + (w->den - 1)) / w->den * w->num * p_dsc->pixel_size;
fine_trace.note: For `VLC_CODEC_YUVP`, VLC uses a packed 1-byte-per-pixel plane. With width 64 and height 384 already aligned to the 16x32 picture constraints, the Y plane ends up with `Y_PITCH=64`, `i_lines=384`, and `i_visible_pitch=64`.

fine_trace.code: if (unlikely(mul_overflow(p->i_pitch, p->i_lines, &plane_sizes[i])) || unlikely(add_overflow(pic_size, plane_sizes[i], &pic_size))) goto error; unsigned char *buf = picture_Allocate(&res->fd, pic_size);
fine_trace.note: Using that single-plane extent, `picture_NewFromFormat()` computes `pic_size = 64 * 384 = 24576` and allocates a 24576-byte Y plane. The saved ASan allocation stack confirms this exact allocation path and size.
The renderer aliases the base of the allocated Y plane as `p_dest`, the pointer used for all later per-pixel writes.

fine_trace.code: bs_init( &bs, p_data->p_buffer + p_sys->i_image_offset + p_sys->second_field_offset, p_data->i_buffer - p_sys->i_image_offset - p_sys->second_field_offset );
fine_trace.note: After the even-field rows finish, the outer `i_field` loop enters the odd-field pass and reinitializes `bs` one byte into the image payload. Static replay of the staged witness shows this second `bs_init()`, not the first one at lines 537-538, feeds the crashing `bs_read()`.

Static replay of the odd-field bitstream shows the crash-driving token occurs on `i_row=383`, `i_column=62`: `bs_read(&bs, 2)` returns color 0 and the next `bs_read(&bs, 2)` returns raw `i_count=2`. In this encoding that token requests a zero-color run of `i_count + 1 = 3` pixels.

Root cause. At the crashing state `p_sys->i_width - i_column = 64 - 62 = 2`, so `__MIN(2, 2)` leaves `i_count` unchanged at 2. The clamp uses the full number of pixels remaining in the row even though the next write covers `i_count + 1` pixels.

Sink. With `i_row=383`, `i_column=62`, `Y_PITCH=64`, and `i_count=2`, this call writes 3 bytes starting at `p_dest[383 * 64 + 62]`, i.e. Y-plane offset 24574. The write covers offsets 24574, 24575, and 24576, so the first invalid byte is exactly the allocation end reported by ASan.

format.name: MPEG Program Stream with SVCD subtitle payload
format.contract: The exact 3150-byte witness must demux into the SVCD subtitle decoder, and `Reassemble()` must expose a complete subtitle block whose header decodes as `p_sys->i_width=64`, `p_sys->i_height=384`, `p_sys->i_image_offset=31`, and `p_sys->second_field_offset=1`. In the odd-field pass of `SVCDSubRenderImage()`, the token at `i_row=383`, `i_column=62` must take the zero-color RLE branch with raw `i_count=2`, so line 549 leaves `i_count` at 2 and line 550 executes `memset(..., 3)` from Y-plane offset 24574.
